summary: A first-person account of attending the finals of the International Esports Championship in the author's city on September 15, 2023, used to explain why competitive gaming has gone from niche hobby to mainstream spectacle. The author points to community and inclusivity, athlete-level skill, large prize pools and sponsorship, school scholarships, and online accessibility as drivers. The piece closes by speculating that virtual and augmented reality could push growth further.
one_line: A firsthand account of the 2023 International Esports Championship finals exploring community, athleticism, money, education and technology behind esports' mainstream rise.
key_facts: The finals of the International Esports Championship were held on September 15, 2023, in the author's own city.
Mike "SonicBoom" Henderson, a college student and devout fan, said esports is about "the sense of being part of something huge" and that attendees are "part of a family."
Julia Wang, a middle-aged mother, brought her son to watch his favorite team and said sharing his excitement was "truly special" even though she doesn't know every game's nuances.
ShadowKnight, real name Alex Ramirez, is a star player who executed a game-changing move during the final, and his team clinched the championship.
The champions' prize was a seven-figure sum plus a gleaming trophy, in contrast to earlier prize pools of game peripherals and modest cash amounts.
Sponsors from both endemic and non-endemic sectors competed for ad space, with logos across the arena and on team jerseys.
The esports ecosystem includes merchandise, media rights, content creation and betting.
Emily Saunders, a representative of a leading gaming hardware company, said esports fans are "tech-savvy, brand-aware, and incredibly loyal."
Vendors at the event sold items ranging from custom gaming chairs to energy drinks.
Schools and universities have begun offering scholarships and creating competitive esports teams, where critical thinking, teamwork and communication are valued.
Live streams and online platforms have democratized participation, letting anyone watch, learn and dream of competing.
After the win, the champions signed autographs and took selfies with fans.
The author expects virtual and augmented reality to drive further esports growth.
